name: Lakeridge Highway
summary: Gnolls and Blackrock orcs make Lakeridge Highway perilous along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Before the First War, the road carried trade through Redridge; now ruin and danger bar the way.

sections.title: A Fallen Artery
sections.body: Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway carried goods and travelers through Redridge along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Travelers crossed between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under Stormwind's protection. Then the Horde marched through, and that safety was shattered. Eastern Redridge remains contested and desolate.

sections.title: Peril on the Road
sections.body: After Blackrock orcs seized Stonewatch Keep, road repairs and patrols ceased. Lakeridge Highway crumbled into an overgrown track, where savage gnoll packs roam. Stormwind's forces are spread thin and cannot reinforce Lakeshire, so the highway remains officially unsafe. Travelers bound for the eastern ridges face gnoll ambushes along the way.

faq.q: Where does the Lakeridge Highway lead?
faq.answer: Lakeridge Highway follows Lake Everstill's southern shore east from Lakeshire toward the foothills around Stonewatch Keep and the eastern mountains of Redridge.

Lakeridge Highway fell into disuse after the First War, especially when Blackrock orcs fortified Stonewatch Keep. Stormwind lacked the forces to secure and maintain the road, leaving hostile gnolls free to move in and civilian travel choked off.

faq.q: What threats wander the road today?
faq.answer: Aggressive gnolls ambush travelers who stray from Lakeshire, while Blackrock orc scouts still operate from the eastern strongholds.
No. Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway was a well-kept, heavily traveled route that safely linked Redridge's heartland with its eastern outposts.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Lakeridge Highway shows how far Stormwind's neglected frontier reaches. Roads just beyond Lakeshire have been left to gnolls and orcs for lack of reinforcements.
